ESKOM INTELLIGENCE

By: Nicky Troll | Delivery

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
Andre De Ruyter's Explosive interviews was the springboard to a media frenzy based on deliberately vague reporting... We uncover why.

Unique Selling Point:
- a big news story
- an alternative more truthful and sensible angle


Summary:
IT's so frustrating when the truth gets in the way of a good story. Crime Cartels. Politicians looting Eskom. Sabotage. It's the stuff journalists dream about.

But that's just what the Eskom Files are... a pipedream without evidence. And at Carte Blanche we don't deal in dreams, our currency is FACTS.

After three weeks of wild speculation and calls for the former Eskom CEO to give names of the alleged criminal behind Eskom's demise - we look at the facts and give an honest reflection on one of the biggest stories of the year so far.


Further information:
The Eskom Files were shared with us and a we promised an exclusive interview. Turns out we were lied to. No interview. Nothing worth reporting on in the so-called intelligence reports.

We tell the alternative less sexy, more truthful version of these illusive reports that De Ruyter seeming based his explosive interview comments on.

We speak to an analyst that is involved with compiling the reports. We hear from a police insider that has knowledge of the police investigation.

This is story will not make us popular with fellow journalists and even some of the the report compilers, but it's the truth and that's all we need.

STRUCTURE: ESKOM FILES

VO: Wanton corruption. Unbridled criminality, misconduct, and neglect. The national power utility is on its knees.

REWIND EFFECT…. TITLE: December 2022
VO: Eskom-CEO Andre De Ruyter steps down saying the job has become untenable.

FAST FORWARD EFFECT…. TITLE: 9 FEBRUARY 2023
VO: President Cyril Ramaphosa declares a state of disaster.

UPSOUND SONA: “The energy crisis is an existential threat to our economy and the social fabric of the country.”

FAST FORWARD EFFECT…. TITLE: 21 FEBRUARY 2023
VO: Then comes an explosive interview.

UPSOUND ANNIKA INTERVIEW
de Ruyter: We know of at least four organized crime cartels operating in Mpumalanga, in Eskom.

de Ruyter: there was one particular high level politician that was involved in this,

VO: A media frenzy follows. It’s reported his allegations are based on secret intelligence reports.

LINK: We've also had sight of these reports. We were also briefed in a confidential meeting. We also spent months interrogating their contents.

VO: The reports, issued monthly, detail an elaborate organogram.

Heading the operation is a top politician - he’s labeled the “territorial ruler”. There’s a “henchman”, “a feared murder squad”, a “propaganda machine”, a “confidant of principals”, a list of high-ranking “corrupt” cops, and also a prominent minister linked to one of four criminal syndicates called ‘cartel’s.

At first glance, these revelations that would sink any government.

2 SECOND BREATHER TO CHANGE SCENE.

VO: The people compiling these reports have been operating in the shadows.

Now, Questions are being asked of them - about their motives, their paymasters - and even about the legitimacy of the reports.

One of the analysts behind the intelligence has agreed to talk.

INSIDER: We can't operate when we are expected. //We put the puzzle together. We can't operate actually in the limelight.

VO: Out of concern for his safety, we’ve made every effort to hide his identity.

INSIDER: it's a matter of you of being wiped away if you are offering any resistance. These are people seeing money only, there is no moral consideration whatsoever. I'm scared like hell.

VO: We've disguised his voice to conceal his identity. As a former national intelligence officer, he’s used to living under the radar.

INSIDER: In this project, we were tasked to work through a different channel towards the client, the client embodied by Mr. de Ruyter // There was a deep frustration that requests directed to law enforcement and security institutions had not delivered substantial results.

VO: For close to a year, a team of privately funded operatives infiltrated Eskom using a network of secret informants.

INSIDER: As the sources and contacts get better placed and better informed, we suddenly realised that we are onto something really substantial.

VO: The reports covered rackets involving bribes for jobs, sabotage, tender fraud, diesel theft, cable theft and operations run by the so-called coal mafia - subjects we’ve often dealt with on Carte Blanche.

LINK: Load shedding has been with us for more than a decade and it seems to only be getting worse. Corruption at Parastatals has been with us for more than a decade, and it certainly is getting worse. Who stands to gain from all of this?

VO: According to political analyst, Dr. Ntsikelelo Breakfast, that’s a mystery easily solved.

BREAKFAST: It's an open secret that Eskom has been used as a centre of accumulation to amass wealth. There have been people who have used both social capital and political capital // And some of those people are linked to the ruling party.
BONGANI: Do you think Eskom is a feeding trough for the ANC.
BREAKFAST: Yes, I think it is a cash cow // Maybe not the whole ANC //But // those people who are prominent within the ANC, who are linked to Eskom, really they do damage the image of the ANC.

VO: De Ruyter's allegations, described as deliberately vague, were denied by the ANC and lambasted by Cabinet Ministers and even the president"

UPSOUND Ramaposa: so that the investigative process can commence so that all of us are then better informed.

VO: More information, claims the president, would end the speculation.

But can it really be dismissed as rumour when the insider sounding the alarm, is the organisation’s CEO? Ben Theron is a Whistleblower Activist.

BEN: ANDRE faces exactly the same problem every whistleblower in the world face is how much information do you share? How do you protect yourself against retaliation?
BEN: When a whistleblower talks out, one of the first things the organization does is to deny, then close ranks. And the third thing they do is to accuse the whistleblower of bringing the company to disrepute.

VO: The ANC’s response to the claims also met with scepticism.

BREAKFAST: // it's discouraging. Their responsiveness indicates a lack of seriousness in addressing the issue// you need to do something about that. You can't fold your arms. // even government itself, they have that responsibility also to uncover the truth in terms of what had happened.

VO: But subsequent media reports have steadfastly avoided identifying the alleged criminals - even though many are named in the intelligence documents. And we know why…

LINK: These are not the Guptaleaks. They're not the Panama Papers. Those had times, places, dates, names, hard evidence. Sure, people are mentioned here, but nothing you can prove. No dots that you can connect.

COP INSIDER: They’re using the word intelligence very loosely. There's a vast difference between intelligence stroke information and actual evidence.

VO: This insider said he’d talk to us as long as we kept his identity secret. He’s linked to the police investigation around Eskom.

BONGANI: Is there anything here that is a lead that could become prosecutable?
COP INSIDER: From what I'm seeing, there's absolutely nothing at this juncture that is prosecutable. // until such a time that it gets converted to actual evidence, affidavits, forensic reports, communication analysis, section 204 statements, 252 operations in terms of the act, until such time that those documents are not contained in a docket. It is what it is. Just information.

VO: Something we can confirm: juicy information but currently uncorroborated.

BONGANI: In one instance, David Mabuza reportedly burnt 2 million rand in cash because he didn't want to have so much hard currency on his person. I'm using these examples to to ask the question for a normal person, they might even say that's just gossip.
INSIDER: So there are many stories about it. We don't throw it away, but we don't follow it up as if it's the truth and the only truth.
BONGANI: In one example you mentioned a Teppo Mabuza, who's the nephew of the now former deputy president David Mabuza. All there is in this report is his age. He's 31. He's got a Ferrari. He's got a Porsche. His wife purportedly has a company that has contracts with Eskom. And then later in the reports, you can't find any companies of which she's a director. Do you see what I mean?
INSIDER: I can't comment on that. At the moment. That can be information hanging, which should be followed up. That's definitely not the end purpose is not to publish rumours like that saying this is the truth and the solid truth.

VO: He admits to needing more time and to the information not being evidence, yet it’s this kind of detail that was included in the now infamous intelligence reports.

BONGANI: How Possible Is it for you not to be used? In other words //I can tell you anything about anyone.
INSIDER: // Why do we want to fabricate information like this where we know our contacts and ourselves are in grave danger? It went through a process of confirming that information from various different other sources, independent sources.

VO: The police insider isn’t convinced.

COP INSIDER: In intelligence circles, You have a scenario where you might have three independent people reporting the same thing, but the actual original source is one person. From what I've seen from that particular report. My view is that it has not been properly verified.

VO: It can’t be denied that Eskom has been targeted by criminal syndicates. But without hard evidence - convictions and sentences are unlikely. That’s a bitter pill for a country gripped by loadshedding.

Even our interview with Dr Breakfast was interrupted, but we powered on in the dark.

BREAKFAST: I don't accept the argument that there is no substantive evidence in terms of what is happening with regard to the institutionalization of corruption at Eskom. we know what is the problem. The problem that we have is the issue of power outage that we have almost each and every day, and we have normalized that.M21 back to front)
BONGANI: In a sense, if we don't have hard evidence that suits those people who want the status quo to remain. That's the indictment, isn't it?
BREAKFAST: I Think you've hit the nail on the head. // it means that nothing must be done because there's no hard evidence. So the status quo must be perpetuated.

VO: Action could and should have been taken sooner - the police had knowledge of these reports.

BONGANI: How high up did that knowledge go?
COP INSIDER: Well, the national commission is aware of it.
COP INSIDER: By now our intelligence services should have been in a position to have instituted or at least initiated covert investigations // where’s the was? Intelligence services like Crime Intelligence, the state security agency whose role it is to inform government about the domestic threats to our constitutional order and national stability.

VO: While the SAPS National Commissioner established a task team and 117 arrests have been made - these are not high level suspects.

It’s also now that feared any investigation may have been blunted by De Ruyter’s interview.

COP INSIDER: All the sleeping dogs have by now wide awake, and those that were awake are more awake.
BONGANI: What happens if no action is taken? What happens if this is just another little blimp in the road but we carry on?
BEN: This is not a blimp. This is a mountain. South Africa's future, this country's future is dependent on Eskom surviving.

BONGANI: Are we sitting ducks?
INSIDER: Anarchy is closer than we think. I'm saying that powerful people. For the wrong reasons. Are mightier than we think. And that is the danger.

VO: In confronting that danger, investigations based on solid intelligence will be needed. In Eskom’s case the most pressing question is: how much of what we know is deliberately vague and how much is simply… speculation?

ENDS



PROMOS

PROMO 1 - 11 seconds
VO: An explosive intelligence report alleging grand corruption and looting inside Eskom - yet none of the people implicated have been named or arrested. Why?

PROMO 2 - 21 seconds
VO: High ranking government ministers and alleged criminal cartels behind the corruption and criminality crippling Eskom - all exposed in damning intelligence reports, but no one behind bars.

COP INSIDER: All the sleeping dogs have by now wide awake, and those that were awake are more awake.

VO: We investigate the impact of this explosive reports.

PROMO 3 - 21 seconds
VO:

With the surfacing of wild allegations about corruption and criminality at Eskom - informants are now at risk.

INSIDER: It's a matter of you of being wiped away if you are offering any resistance. These are people seeing money only, there is no moral consideration whatsoever.
